chunks: Yunus narrated from Sama'ah from Abu Basir who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would flog the free man and the slave, the Jew and the Christian, for wine and nabidh [fermented drink] eighty [strikes]. So I said, 'What is the matter with the Jew and the Christian and Jew?' He said, 'When they manifest that in a province among the provinces, because it is not for them to manifest its drinking.'
ai.seo_question: What is the flogging penalty for non-Muslims consuming intoxicants in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) clarifies that the eighty-strike penalty for non-Muslims (Ahl al-Kitab) applies specifically when they publicly consume intoxicants within Islamic territories, distinguishing this from the general rule for Muslims. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that their consumption of wine is a violation of their covenantal status as dhimmis, who are expected to adhere to certain public norms of the Islamic state. The narration underscores the link between public visibility and legal accountability in classical fiqh.
